source.title: FON: A Draft-Revise Dual-Organ Language Model without Sequence-Level Quadratic Attention
source.authors: He-Long Hu; Hong Pan; S. Campus; Guangdong Ocean University; Zhanjiang; Guangdong; China; M. S. Center; Maoming; China Pacific Insurance Co.; Ltd. Foshan Branch; Foshan

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports held-out perplexity at two model-width tiers, which bears narrowly on loss versus parameter scale, but it does not reproduce or fit the original power-law measurement.
record.gate_note: The scale-consistency tables report perplexity for models at approximately 30M and 70M parameters. They do not fit a power law or report loss sweeps over tokens or compute; no results test extrapolation from small runs or compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper (FON vs Transformer/Mamba2 on WikiText-103). Perplexity appears at only two width tiers (~30M d256, ~70M d512), with different architectures and an undertrained budget of about 2.7 tokens/param. No loss-versus-scale curve, power-law fit, token or compute sweep, extrapolation test or allocation analysis is reported. Kaplan et al. is cited only to say results are reported per tier without extrapolation. Hoffmann et al. is cited only for the ~20 tokens/param compute-optimal reference, used to declare the undertrained regime. Two points per architecture cannot show or refute a power-law form, so the study does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the scale section. The main conclusion is broader. At the 30M–70M undertrained tier, the drafting/revising dual-organ FON beats Transformer and Mamba2 at iso-parameter and iso-token budgets, and beats all depth-aligned controls. It keeps an O(1) decode state and extrapolates about 8–9% worse at 8x length without positional engineering. The revision organ adds in-domain infilling ability but no perplexity gain. The advantage narrows from d256 to d512 but does not reverse; the authors call this a two-point observation not supporting extrapolation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and compares a new dual-organ architecture on WikiText-103 at two width tiers; it does not use the original scaling-law fitting procedure or report fitted exponents.

fits_no_version.finding: FON's perplexity advantage over a Transformer narrows from d256 (~30M, -35.9% for T2) to d512 (~70M, -22.8% T2 / -20.8% T1) without reversing. This is a two-point observation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative architecture advantages over Transformers shrink as parameter count grows.

record.code_released: The paper says the experimental code will be open-sourced; no URL is stated.
record.problems: Only two model-width tiers are reported; the paper states the models are in an undertrained regime (about 2.7 tokens per parameter) and does not support extrapolation to larger scales. The d512 synthetic-data convention is not stated in the scale-consistency table.

untested.parts: No power-law fit; only two parameter tiers (~2x apart) per architecture; no token or compute sweep; undertrained regime.
No extrapolation from small runs; the authors explicitly decline to extrapolate.
No compute-optimal allocation analysis; the Chinchilla ratio is cited only as a reference.
Depth-aligned Transformer baselines (L8/L10) change the parameter count and are single-seed method comparisons, not a fixed-parameter shape sweep.
Not addressed; LAMBADA is noted as uninformative at 30M.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 and the V1 limits_scope label are not justified. Two tiers of an architecture comparison carry no information about the power-law form, and a 'not tested' situation should not produce a limits_scope label. All rows relinked to none. Table 3 omits the p_synth convention, so d256 and d512 values may not be directly comparable.

versions.untested_parts: Only two model-width tiers are reported, not several orders of magnitude. The study does not fit a power law and does not sweep tokens or compute.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The paper's d256 and d512 scale comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Perplexity is reported at only two tiers and the paper explicitly does not linearly extrapolate; these results do not establish the claimed power-law form or its behavior over several orders of magnitude (r1–r8).
